precepts.text: The Most High created a new thing in the earth, a woman shall compass a man; Vashti compassing the king is the very thing the wise men move to stop before it spreads.
precepts.point: But the queen Vashti refused to come at the king's commandment by his chamberlains, and the king was very wroth and his anger burned in him. She disrespected the king before everyone, and a judgment was now set to come.

note.label: Esther 1: Vashti Refuses the King and the Law of Order in the House

precepts.why:
“How long wilt thou go about, O thou backsliding daughter? for the Lord hath created a new thing in the earth, A woman shall compass a man.” The Most High created a new thing in the earth: a woman shall compass a man.

That is Vashti. The king commanded his seven chamberlains “To bring Vashti the queen before the king with the crown royal, to shew the people and the princes her beauty”, and “the queen Vashti refused to come at the king’s commandment by his chamberlains”. She disrespected the king before everyone, a woman compassing a man, and “therefore was the king very wroth, and his anger burned in him.”

Vashti compassing the king is the very thing the wise men move to stop before it spreads, and a judgment was now set to come.

precepts.text: Things left wanting are to be set in order, which is the work of restoring the house to its right order that this chapter puts into a decree.
precepts.point: This order, that every man should bear rule in his own house, is set up in the Bible for the man, and it is the very order the Most High established that the societies of the earth keep reversing.

note.label: Esther 1: Vashti Refuses the King and the Law of Order in the House

precepts.why:
“the saying pleased the king and the princes; and the king did according to the word of Memucan”. Letters went “into all the king’s provinces, into every province according to the writing thereof, and to every people after their language, that every man should bear rule in his own house”. What Vashti did had left something wanting in every house of the kingdom, and the decree is the setting of it back in order.

That is the very work Paul left Titus in Crete to do: “that thou shouldest set in order the things that are wanting, and ordain elders in every city”. Where things are wanting, they are not left as they are; they are set in order. The house has a right order, and restoring it is a work that has to be done and published.

The order that “every man should bear rule in his own house” is set up in the Bible for the man. It is the order the Most High established, and it is the very order the societies of the earth keep reversing. This chapter puts the restoring of it into a decree, published in the language of every people.

precepts.text: Where the order is out of course, children become the people's oppressors and women rule over them, the reversal of the house the Most High warns against.
precepts.point: This order, that every man should bear rule in his own house, is set up in the Bible for the man, and it is the very order the Most High established that the societies of the earth keep reversing.

note.label: Esther 1: Vashti Refuses the King and the Law of Order in the House

precepts.why:
The decree that “every man should bear rule in his own house” is the Most High's order for the house. Isaiah shows what it looks like when that order is out of course: “As for my people, children are their oppressors, and women rule over them.” The children become the people's oppressors and the women rule over them; the house is turned upside down.

“O my people, they which lead thee cause thee to err, and destroy the way of thy paths.” When the wrong ones are leading, the people are led into error and the way of their paths is destroyed. That is the reversal the Most High warns against, and it is the reversal the societies of the earth keep making of the order he established.

So the letters sent to every province, published in the language of every people, set the house the right way up: the man bears rule in his own house, as it is set up in the Bible for him.

points: Ahasuerus reigned from India unto Ethiopia over 127 provinces, and the power of Persia and Media stood before him. This is the same land where Mordecai and Hadassah were, which we are about to celebrate at Purim.
In the days of Ahasuerus, who reigned from India even unto Ethiopia over a hundred and twenty seven provinces, the king sat on the throne of his kingdom in Shushan the palace.

note.label: Esther 1: Vashti Refuses the King and the Law of Order in the House

points: In the third year of his reign he made a feast unto all his princes and servants, the power of Persia and Media, the nobles and princes of the provinces being before him.

note.label: Esther 1: Vashti Refuses the King and the Law of Order in the House

points: The king showed the riches of his glorious kingdom and the honour of his excellent majesty for many days, even a hundred and fourscore days, showing out for a full hundred and eighty days.

note.label: Esther 1: Vashti Refuses the King and the Law of Order in the House

points: When those days were expired he made a feast of seven days for all the people present in Shushan, with white, green, and blue hangings, beds of gold and silver, and royal wine in abundance, and the drinking was according to the law, none did compel, every man doing according to his pleasure.

note.label: Esther 1: Vashti Refuses the King and the Law of Order in the House

points: Vashti the queen also made a feast for the women in the royal house belonging to the king. On the seventh day, when the heart of the king was merry with wine, he commanded his seven chamberlains to bring Vashti before him with the crown royal to show the people and princes her beauty, for she was fair to look on.

note.label: Esther 1: Vashti Refuses the King and the Law of Order in the House

points: But the queen Vashti refused to come at the king's commandment by his chamberlains, and the king was very wroth and his anger burned in him. She disrespected the king before everyone, and a judgment was now set to come.

note.label: Esther 1: Vashti Refuses the King and the Law of Order in the House

points: The king turned to the wise men who knew the times, for so was the king's manner toward all that knew law and judgment, and the seven princes of Persia and Media who saw the king's face and sat first in the kingdom were next to him.

note.label: Esther 1: Vashti Refuses the King and the Law of Order in the House

points: He asked what should be done unto the queen Vashti according to law, because she had not performed the commandment of the king by the chamberlains. A judgment had to be rendered because she disrespected him in front of everybody.

note.label: Esther 1: Vashti Refuses the King and the Law of Order in the House

points: Memucan answered before the king and the princes that Vashti had not done wrong to the king only, but also to all the princes and all the people in all the provinces of the king.

note.label: Esther 1: Vashti Refuses the King and the Law of Order in the House

points: The deed of the queen would come abroad unto all women, so that they would despise their husbands in their eyes, saying the king commanded Vashti and she came not; likewise the ladies of Persia and Media would say the same that day, and there would arise too much contempt and wrath.

note.label: Esther 1: Vashti Refuses the King and the Law of Order in the House

points: Memucan advised the king to let a royal commandment go from him, written among the laws of the Persians and Medes that it be not altered, that Vashti come no more before the king, and that he give her royal estate unto another better than she.

note.label: Esther 1: Vashti Refuses the King and the Law of Order in the House

points: When the king's decree was published throughout all his empire, for it was great, all the wives would give their husbands honour, both to great and small. Vashti loses her estate so that the order of the house would be upheld everywhere.

note.label: Esther 1: Vashti Refuses the King and the Law of Order in the House

points: The saying pleased the king and the princes, and the king did according to the word of Memucan, sending letters into all his provinces, to every province and people after their language, that every man should bear rule in his own house.
This order, that every man should bear rule in his own house, is set up in the Bible for the man, and it is the very order the Most High established that the societies of the earth keep reversing.
